concerns.text: HumanEval reference solutions are Python, not C/C++. FR-002 mandates gcc/clang compilation and the fuzzing pipeline (libFuzzer/AFL++) presupposes C/C++ binaries. The assumption 'HumanEval or Codeforces datasets contain … executable C/C++ reference solutions' is factually wrong for HumanEval. The dataset must be restricted to sources with C/C++ references (e.g., Codeforces C++ submissions) or the pipeline redesigned; otherwise the foundational paired dataset cannot exist.

The design is PAIRED (each problem has one human and one LLM solution, per ProblemPair), but FR-005/SC-001 specify Mann-Whitney U and KS, which treat groups as independent and discard the pairing. The correct primary test for paired per-problem crash counts is Wilcoxon signed-rank (or a paired permutation test); using unpaired tests on paired data loses power and misstates the dependence structure.

libFuzzer/AFL++ require a per-snippet coverage-instrumented harness (LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput) and sanitizer builds; 'supply random inputs to all exposed functions' is not how these fuzzers operate on arbitrary challenge binaries. The spec never requires harness generation or ASan/UBSan instrumentation, without which most memory-safety bugs will NOT crash and crash_count is a near-floor, biased proxy. Also, crashes on random inputs to algorithmic challenge code often reflect unhandled input assumptions, not security vulnerabilities — construct validity of 'crash count = security posture' needs explicit justification or a triage step distinguishing security-relevant crashes.

Crash count and severity score are not independent metrics: severity is assigned per crash via the triage rubric (FR-004), so severity distributions are mechanically coupled to crash counts. Treating them as two hypotheses under one multiple-comparison correction overstates the evidence of distinct findings; the spec should acknowledge this coupling or define severity as a per-problem aggregate with an explicitly independent derivation.

'reports zero crashes for the safe one' conflates absence of detected crashes with safety — a fuzzer finding no crash in a bounded window is weak evidence. Rephrase the test expectation as 'no crash within the budget' rather than implying verification of safety.
